advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Compare the resolved/normalized scratch base (e.g. `base.resolve()` or `os.path.realpath`) against the canonical mount rather than relying on exact lexical `Path` equality of the raw env value.
evidence: src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py:104: `return os.environ.get("REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR") or ""` — the base is the raw env string, never `resolve()`d or normalized

A miss on this membership-style comparison is silent: `not (declared or configured_dedicated_path)` returns `None` (admit), so a mismatched spelling of the same dedicated volume is indistinguishable from a host that genuinely has no dedicated scratch volume — the check fails open.
advisory.finding: The new canonical-path arming uses exact `Path` equality (`base == _CANONICAL_GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT`) against a path built directly from the raw, unresolved `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` env value, so any non-canonical-but-equivalent spelling (symlinked ancestor, `..`, `//`) fails to match and the guard silently reverts to the old admit-on-root behavior.
scenarios: REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR set to a symlinked path or one with a trailing `..`/`//` that resolves to /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch but is not lexically equal
A host where /var/lib is a symlink

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for the configured canonical path with proof marker present but declaration absent (monkeypatch `_CANONICAL_GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT` to `host.base`, `host.mount()`, no `host.declare()`) asserting the gate ADMITS.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/gate_admission.py:202-206: `configured_dedicated_path = base == _CANONICAL_GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT` then `if not (declared or configured_dedicated_path): return None` then `if (base / _SCRATCH_MOUNTED_MARKER).is_file(): return None` — before this diff line 205 was only reachable when declared=True; the added disjunct makes `configured=True, declared=False, proof present` newly reach the admit path.

Named violating input: monkeypatch `_CANONICAL_GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT` to `host.base`, call `host.mount()` (proof present) WITHOUT `host.declare()`; the gate must admit. No test in test_gate_scratch_volume_aa40.py constructs this state — `test_configured_dedicated_scratch_path_refuses_without_markers` (line 148) sets no mounted marker, and `test_proof_without_declaration_also_admits` (line 168) does not monkeypatch the canonical path.
ABSENCE: a refactor moving/altering the mounted-marker check relative to the configured/declared disjunction could regress the configured-path-with-proof admit case undetected.
advisory.finding: The new `configured_dedicated_path` disjunct makes a new state reachable at the mounted-marker short-circuit — canonical configured path, declaration absent, proof marker PRESENT — which now resolves to ADMIT, but no test exercises it. The added test only covers the both-markers-absent refusal.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a sibling to `test_configured_dedicated_scratch_path_refuses_without_markers` that additionally calls `host.mount()` and asserts `ga.gate_admission(...)` runs the body (admits), pinning that the proof marker still short-circuits refusal on the configured canonical path.
